choices.label: A
choices.text: Establish base System Architecture and design, install version control and continuous integration setup.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0; architecture, version control and CI are set up while delivering value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There is no such thing as Sprint 0.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Sprint 0; every Sprint delivers a usable Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Base System Architecture and design.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0 dedicated to architecture.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overall planning, base System Architecture, base design, version control and continuous integration setup.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0 dedicated to planning and setup.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Requirements gathering, version control setup, and continuous integration setup.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0 dedicated to requirements and setup.

questions.question:
Product Backlog Items are refined by:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers take part, but not alone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner takes part, but not alone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Refinement is a collaboration of the whole Scrum Team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Business Analyst and the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Business Analyst role.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for the System Architecture of a Product being developed using Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Architect chosen by the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no architect role; the Developers are responsible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers are responsible for the system architecture.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Software Architect.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Software Architect role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Corporate Architect.
choices.explanation: A corporate architect outside the team is not responsible.

questions.question:
Which of the following are attributes of a bad bug report?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Simple and repeatable reproduction steps.
choices.explanation: Simple, repeatable reproduction steps make a good bug report.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vague statements or untested assumptions.
choices.explanation: Vague statements make the bug hard to understand and reproduce.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Generic titles.
choices.explanation: Generic titles make bugs hard to find and triage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: One bug per report.
choices.explanation: One bug per report is a good practice.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Assigning blame.
choices.explanation: Blaming people harms collaboration and does not help fix the bug.

questions.question:
When Developers are having trouble delivering an Increment because they do not understand a functional requirement, what should they do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Partially complete the functionality, and discuss the remaining work at the Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: Partially done work is not part of the Increment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a specialist to the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Adding people is not the first answer to a misunderstanding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Collaborate with the Product Owner to determine what is possible and acceptable.
choices.explanation: Developers collaborate with the Product Owner to find what is possible and acceptable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Defer the work to a more appropriate Sprint.
choices.explanation: Deferring the work does not solve the misunderstanding.

questions.question:
Who should be present during Product Backlog Refinement?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The integration architects from the release department.
choices.explanation: Refinement is not reserved to architects from another department.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only the most senior Developers.
choices.explanation: All Developers can contribute, not only the senior ones.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Anyone that the Scrum Team decides will be valuable during Refinement.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team decides who can bring value to refinement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Stakeholders can be invited, but they are not required.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The external Business Analysts that have prepared the functional details.
choices.explanation: Refinement is done by the Scrum Team, not by external analysts.

questions.question: True or False: Programmers and Testers should not be included in refining Product Backlog Items.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Everyone doing the work, including programming and testing skills, should take part in refinement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Developers, whatever their skills, contribute to refinement.

questions.question:
Upon what type of process control is Scrum based?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Defined.
choices.explanation: Defined processes are the opposite of Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Empirical.
choices.explanation: Scrum is founded on empirical process control.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complex.
choices.explanation: Complex describes the problem, not the process control.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hybrid.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not hybrid.

questions.question:
When might a Sprint be abnormally cancelled?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
choices.explanation: A Sprint may be cancelled by the Product Owner when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the sales department has an important new opportunity.
choices.explanation: A new opportunity goes to the Product Backlog; it does not justify cancellation by itself.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the Developers feel that the work is too hard.
choices.explanation: Difficulty is not a reason to cancel; scope can be renegotiated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When it becomes clear that not everything will be finished by the end of the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Not finishing everything is handled by renegotiating scope.

questions.question:
Who should know the most about the progress toward a business objective or a release, and be able to explain the alternatives most clearly?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not the most knowledgeable about business progress.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner knows the progress toward business objectives.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers know the progress within the Sprint, not toward business objectives.

questions.question:
When many Scrum Teams are working on a single Product, what best describes the Definition of Done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each Scrum Team defines and uses its own. The differences are discussed and reconciled during a hardening Sprint.
choices.explanation: Hardening Sprints do not exist in Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Masters from each Scrum Team define a common Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is set by the Scrum Teams, not by the Scrum Masters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each Scrum Team uses its own, but must make their definition clear to all other teams so the differences are known.
choices.explanation: Separate definitions do not guarantee that the combined work is releasable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All Scrum Teams must have a Definition of Done that makes their combined Increment valuable and useful.
choices.explanation: Teams on the same product share a Definition of Done ensuring their integrated work is releasable.

questions.question:
When is a Sprint over?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When all Product Backlog Items meet their Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: The Sprint does not end when items are done; it is timeboxed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the timebox expires.
choices.explanation: A Sprint ends when its timebox expires.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the Product Owner says it is done.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not end the Sprint arbitrarily.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When all the tasks are completed.
choices.explanation: Completing tasks does not end the Sprint.

questions.question:
When does the next Sprint begin?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immediately following the next Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is part of the Sprint; the Sprint does not start after it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint.
choices.explanation: A new Sprint starts immediately after the previous one ends.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the Product Owner is ready.
choices.explanation: The start of a Sprint does not depend on the Product Owner's readiness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Next Monday.
choices.explanation: Sprints do not wait for a specific weekday.

questions.question:
What does it mean to say that an event has a timebox?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The event must happen at a set time.
choices.explanation: A timebox refers to duration, not to the scheduled start time of the event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The event can take no more than a maximum amount of time.
choices.explanation: A timebox establishes a maximum duration that the event cannot exceed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The event must happen by a given time.
choices.explanation: A timebox limits how long the event can last, not when it must be completed by.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The event must take at least a minimum amount of time.
choices.explanation: A timebox sets an upper limit, not a required minimum duration.

questions.question:
Who is required to attend the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers and Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is not required.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers and Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master and Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master and Product Owner are not required.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Only the Developers are required, not the whole Scrum Team.

questions.question:
When does a Developer become accountable for the value of a Product Backlog Item selected for the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever a team member can accommodate more work.
choices.explanation: Capacity does not create individual accountability for value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the Sprint Planning Event.
choices.explanation: Selecting items at Sprint Planning does not make an individual accountable for value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: During the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum does not assign individual accountability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Never. The entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating value every Sprint.
choices.explanation: The entire Scrum Team is accountable for creating a valuable, useful Increment every Sprint.

questions.question:
Who is on the Scrum Team?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Project Manager.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team does not include a Project Manager role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers are one of the three accountabilities on the Scrum Team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is a member of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is a member of the Scrum Team.

questions.question:
The timebox for the Sprint Review is:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: As long as needed.
choices.explanation: Events are timeboxed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 2 hours.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is 4 hours for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 4 hours for a monthly Sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is at most 4 hours for a one-month Sprint, usually shorter for shorter Sprints.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 4 hours and longer as needed.
choices.explanation: The timebox cannot be exceeded.

choices.label: E
choices.text: 1 day.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is not one day.

questions.question:
The timebox for the Sprint Planning event is?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: 8 hours for a monthly Sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is at most 8 hours for a one-month Sprint, usually shorter for shorter Sprints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 4 hours.
choices.explanation: Four hours is the Sprint Review timebox.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever it is done.
choices.explanation: Events are timeboxed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Monthly.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is held every Sprint.

questions.question: True or False: The purpose of a Sprint is to produce a valuable and useful Increment of working Product.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide states that each Sprint results in a usable, valuable Increment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide defines the Sprint as producing a usable, valuable Increment.

questions.question:
An organization has decided to adopt Scrum, but Management wants to change the terminology to fit with terminology already used. What will likely happen if this is done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Without a new vocabulary as a reminder of the change, very little change may actually happen.
choices.explanation: Without new vocabulary, little change may actually happen.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The organization may not understand what has changed with Scrum and the benefits of Scrum may be lost.
choices.explanation: The benefits of Scrum may be lost if what changed is not understood.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Management may feel less anxious.
choices.explanation: Management may feel less anxious, but that hides the change.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: All these consequences can occur.

questions.question:
Who creates the Definition of Done?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Team, in a collaborative effort where the result is the common denominator of all members' definitions.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is not a common denominator of personal definitions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master since they are responsible for the productivity of the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not create it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner since they are responsible for the Product's success.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not create it alone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If it is not an organizational standard, the Scrum Team must create a Definition of Done appropriate for the Product.
choices.explanation: If it is not an organizational standard, the Scrum Team creates a Definition of Done appropriate for the product.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for managing the progress of work during a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers manage their own progress during the Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The most junior member of the team.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no hierarchy among Developers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not manage the Developers' work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not manage the Developers' work.

questions.question:
Which Scrum events are timeboxed?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Release Retrospective.
choices.explanation: There is no Release Retrospective in Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sprint Planning.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is timeboxed to eight hours for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Testing.
choices.explanation: There is no testing Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refinement.
choices.explanation: Refinement is an activity, not a timeboxed event.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is timeboxed to three hours for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is timeboxed to four hours for a one-month Sprint.

choices.label: G
choices.text: Release Testing.
choices.explanation: Release Testing is not a Scrum event.

questions.question:
When does a Developer become the sole owner of a Sprint Backlog item?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever a team member can accommodate more work.
choices.explanation: No individual owns Sprint Backlog items.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum does not assign ownership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the Sprint Planning event.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning does not assign ownership.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Never. All Sprint Backlog items are "owned" by the Developers on the Scrum Team even though each item may be implemented by an individual Developer.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Backlog belongs to the Developers collectively, even if one person implements an item.

questions.question:
Why is the Daily Scrum held at the same time and same place?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The consistency reduces complexity.
choices.explanation: Holding it at the same time and place reduces complexity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The place can be named.
choices.explanation: Naming the place is not the reason.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner demands it.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not demand it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rooms are hard to book and this lets it be booked in advance.
choices.explanation: Room booking is a convenience, not the reason.

questions.question:
The length of a Sprint should be:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Short enough to keep the business risk acceptable to the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Shorter Sprints limit business risk.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Short enough to be able to synchronize the development work with other business events.
choices.explanation: Sprints can be aligned with business events.

choices.label: C
choices.text: One month or less.
choices.explanation: Sprints are one month or less.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All of the above.
choices.explanation: All these considerations apply.

questions.question:
How much work must the Developers complete for each Product Backlog Item they select for a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enough so that each Product Backlog Item they select meets the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: Each selected item must meet the Definition of Done.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Analysis, design, programming, testing and documentation.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe phases.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As much as it can fit into the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Work is not deferred; it is Done or returns to the Product Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All development work and at least some testing.
choices.explanation: Some testing is not enough; the Definition of Done defines the full quality.

questions.question:
What is the recommended size for a Scrum Team?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Minimum of 7.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not set a minimum of 7.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require exactly 9.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Typically 10 or fewer people.
choices.explanation: A Scrum Team is typically 10 or fewer people.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 7 plus or minus 2.
choices.explanation: This is an old rule; the current Scrum Guide says 10 or fewer.

questions.question:
Which statement best describes a Product Owner's responsibility?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep Stakeholders from distracting the Developers.
choices.explanation: Shielding Developers from stakeholders is primarily a Scrum Master concern, not the core accountability of the Product Owner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Optimizing the value of the work the Scrum Team does.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Managing the project and ensuring that the work meets the commitments to the Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner focuses on maximizing value, not guaranteeing commitments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Directing the Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers are self-managing and are not directed by the Product Owner.

questions.question: True or False: 100% Code Coverage of tests guarantees bug-free Software.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Coverage only shows that code was executed, not that it behaves correctly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Even 100% coverage cannot guarantee bug-free software: tests may miss cases or assert the wrong thing.

questions.question:
Who can tell the Developers what to work on?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog and so determines what the Developers work on next.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The COO, CEO and CTO.
choices.explanation: Managers do not direct the Developers' work in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not tell the Developers what to work on.

questions.question:
SCRUM stands for:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Super Creative Really Useful Method.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not an acronym.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Self Organising Collaborative & Reflective Universal Method.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not an acronym.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Safe Controlled Response Under Management.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not an acronym.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nothing. It's not an acronym.
choices.explanation: Scrum is a term borrowed from rugby, not an acronym.

questions.question:
Bugs discovered out of Sprint should be:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Investigated and fixed immediately by the Developers.
choices.explanation: Bugs in already delivered work are new work; the Product Owner decides when to address them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reviewed with the Product Owner and added to the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Bugs found outside the Sprint become Product Backlog items ordered by the Product Owner.

questions.question:
When could a release to Production occur if a Scrum Team produced a Done increment multiple times each day?
(choose the best four answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mid Sprint.
choices.explanation: A Done Increment can be released in the middle of a Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every Sprint.
choices.explanation: Releasing every Sprint is possible.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multiple times per day.
choices.explanation: Several releases per day are possible if Done Increments are created several times a day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every Day.
choices.explanation: Daily releases are possible.

questions.question: True or False: The Definition of Done is a mandatory part of Scrum.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is mandatory.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Definition of Done is the commitment for the Increment, mandatory in Scrum.

questions.question: True or False: A Scrum Team must be 10 or fewer people.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Guide says 'typically 10 or fewer', not a strict rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team is typically 10 or fewer people, but this is not an absolute rule.

questions.question:
Sizing is best when:
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is done by the actual Developers who will carry out the work.
choices.explanation: Those who will do the work are best placed to size it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is done by a group, rather than an individual.
choices.explanation: Group sizing combines perspectives and reduces bias.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estimates are made relative to similar things.
choices.explanation: Relative sizing compared to known items is easier and more accurate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is done by the Lead Developer alone.
choices.explanation: There is no Lead Developer sizing alone in Scrum.

questions.question:
Select the correct timebox for each Scrum event.
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 8 hours or less, Daily Scrum - 30 minutes or less, Sprint Review - 4 hours or less, Sprint Retrospective - 3 hours or less.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is 15 minutes, not 30.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 4 hours or less, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes or less, Sprint Review - 8 hours or less, Sprint Retrospective - 4 hours or less.
choices.explanation: Sprint Review is 4 hours, not 8.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 4 hours or less, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes or less, Sprint Review - 4 hours or less, Sprint Retrospective - 4 hours or less.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning is 8 hours and the Retrospective 3 hours.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sprint Planning - 8 hours or less, Daily Scrum - 15 minutes or less, Sprint Review - 4 hours or less, Sprint Retrospective - 3 hours or less.
choices.explanation: These are the correct maximum timeboxes for a one-month Sprint.

questions.question: True or False: Planning Poker must be used by Scrum Teams.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Planning Poker is optional; Scrum does not prescribe estimation techniques.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require Planning Poker.

questions.question:
What is Test Driven Development?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Appointing the QA Tester as the Lead Developer.
choices.explanation: TDD is not about roles.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The practice of writing Unit Tests prior to writing the implementation code.
choices.explanation: TDD is writing unit tests before the code that satisfies them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Integrating Testers and Developers.
choices.explanation: TDD is not about team composition.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The process of motivating Testers.
choices.explanation: TDD is not about motivation.

questions.question: True or False: Tasks in a Sprint Backlog must be estimated in days/hours.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require any estimate of tasks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Tasks are optional and Scrum does not prescribe how to estimate them.

questions.question:
Bugs discovered in Sprint should be:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fixed immediately.
choices.explanation: A bug in the work of the current Sprint is part of getting it Done, so it is fixed immediately.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ignored if not created by me.
choices.explanation: Every Developer is accountable for quality, whoever created the bug.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Send to the Junior Developer to fix.
choices.explanation: There is no hierarchy deciding who fixes bugs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Added to the bug tracking repository and left for a later Sprint.
choices.explanation: Leaving it for later creates undone work and technical debt.

questions.question: True or False: YAGNI states that most systems work best if they are kept simple rather than made complicated.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: That statement is KISS; YAGNI means not building something until it is actually needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: YAGNI is about not implementing functionality before it is needed; keeping things simple is KISS.

questions.question:
Which one is a Scrum Value?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Focus.
choices.explanation: Focus is a Scrum value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Commitment.
choices.explanation: Commitment is a Scrum value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Courage.
choices.explanation: Courage is a Scrum value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Creativity.
choices.explanation: Creativity is not one of the five Scrum values.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Accountability.
choices.explanation: Accountability is important, but it is not one of the five Scrum values.

questions.question:
What is NOT the name of the original program in source control from which branches are taken?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mainline.
choices.explanation: Mainline is a name for the main line of development.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Feature.
choices.explanation: Feature refers to a branch taken from the main line, not to the main line itself.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trunk.
choices.explanation: Trunk is a name for the main line.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Master.
choices.explanation: Master is a name for the main line.

questions.question:
What is Static Analysis?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Analysis performed on code in a non-runtime environment.
choices.explanation: Static analysis examines code without running it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Analysis performed on Software at runtime.
choices.explanation: Analysis at runtime is dynamic analysis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Duties of a Business Analyst.
choices.explanation: It is not about business analysis.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Checking static classes' readability.
choices.explanation: It is not about static classes.

questions.question:
Which one is true about Black-box testing?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tester can see inside the component or system under test.
choices.explanation: Seeing inside is white-box testing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tests that are done can be either functional or non-functional.
choices.explanation: Black-box tests can be functional or non-functional.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The internal structure of the item being tested is known to the Tester.
choices.explanation: Knowing the internal structure is white-box testing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tester cannot see inside the component or system under test.
choices.explanation: In black-box testing the tester does not see the internals.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The internal structure of the item being tested is not known to the Tester.
choices.explanation: Black-box testing treats the internal structure as unknown.

questions.question:
Which expression is NOT used for KISS principle?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Keep it simple, silly.
choices.explanation: This is a common expansion of KISS.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Keep it safe and same.
choices.explanation: This is not an expansion of KISS.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Keep it small and simple.
choices.explanation: This is a common expansion of KISS.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep it simple stupid.
choices.explanation: This is the original expansion of KISS.

questions.question:
What shapes can be an Architecture Spike?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A prototype which will be thrown away.
choices.explanation: A spike can be a throwaway prototype built only to learn.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A comprehensive architecture implementation.
choices.explanation: A spike is small and focused, not a comprehensive implementation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A quick and dirty implementation.
choices.explanation: A spike can be a quick and dirty implementation built to resolve a technical question.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A plan for all required architectures of the Product.
choices.explanation: A spike is not an upfront plan of all architectures.

questions.question:
What does cross-functionality mean in a Scrum Team?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Each Developer who has a special skill and works with all Scrum Teams of the organization is cross-functional.
choices.explanation: A specialist shared by all teams is not what cross-functionality means.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers should collaborate with all other functional departments of the organization.
choices.explanation: Collaborating with departments does not make the team cross-functional.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers should have all required skills to create potentially releasable Increments without any dependency to others outside the team.
choices.explanation: The Developers together have all the skills needed to create usable Increments, without depending on outsiders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Each Developer should have all required skills to create potentially releasable Increments without any dependency to others outside the team.
choices.explanation: Cross-functionality is a property of the team, not of each individual.

questions.question:
What is the proper reaction of the Developers in the middle of the Sprint when they found they have over committed?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: They should ask the Product Owner to cancel the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Only the Product Owner can cancel, and overcommitment is not a reason.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They extend the Sprint duration.
choices.explanation: Sprints are never extended.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They can add new team members to the team.
choices.explanation: Adding people mid-Sprint usually slows the team down.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They negotiate with the Product Owner about the scope of the Sprint Backlog Items.
choices.explanation: The Developers renegotiate the scope with the Product Owner while keeping the Sprint Goal.

questions.question: True or False: Through Depth of Inheritance metric, a low number for depth implies less complexity but also the possibility of less code reuse through inheritance.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: This statement about depth of inheritance is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: A shallow inheritance tree is simpler but offers fewer reuse opportunities through inheritance.

questions.question:
Which concept has interactive attribute?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sketch.
choices.explanation: A sketch is a quick low-fidelity drawing, not interactive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mockup.
choices.explanation: A mockup is a static visual design.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Wireframe.
choices.explanation: A wireframe shows structure, not interaction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prototype.
choices.explanation: A prototype is interactive, so users can try it.

questions.question: True or False: Afferent Coupling measures the number of classes on which a given class depends.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Afferent coupling counts the classes that depend on a given class; the number of classes it depends on is efferent coupling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The statement describes efferent coupling, not afferent coupling.

questions.question:
Which concerns are most important in the scaled Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Minimizing or removing dependencies between teams.
choices.explanation: Minimizing dependencies between teams is a key concern when scaling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Creating an integrated releasable Increment at the end of each Sprint.
choices.explanation: All teams must create one integrated, releasable Increment every Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Having same Sprint duration for all teams.
choices.explanation: Teams can have different Sprint lengths.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increasing all team members utilization.
choices.explanation: Utilization is not a goal.

questions.question:
How much time should the Product Owner spend on Product Backlog Refinement?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: No more than 10%.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not set a fixed percentage for the Product Owner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No more than 20%.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not set a fixed percentage for the Product Owner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is not the Product Owner responsibility.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, including its refinement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any time that the Product Owner needs.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner spends whatever time is needed on refinement.

questions.question:
Which one is NOT a Test Double?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Two combined Unit Tests.
choices.explanation: Combining unit tests does not create a test double.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Test Spy.
choices.explanation: A test spy is a test double that records calls.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Test Stub.
choices.explanation: A test stub is a test double that returns predefined answers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mock Object.
choices.explanation: A mock object is a test double that verifies interactions.

questions.question:
Which is true about Refactoring?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Through it, the internal structure of code is altered.
choices.explanation: Refactoring changes the internal structure of code.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its results are improved maintainability, code readability and reduced complexity.
choices.explanation: Refactoring improves maintainability and readability and reduces complexity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There should be special and distinct Sprints called “Refactoring Sprint” to do Refactoring with focus every a few Sprints.
choices.explanation: Refactoring is continuous; there are no special Refactoring Sprints.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Through it, the external behavior of code is altered.
choices.explanation: Refactoring keeps the external behavior unchanged.

questions.question:
What are the most important things for increasing transparency?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Using chat tools to have the best communication.
choices.explanation: Chat tools help communication but do not create transparency on the work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Having a Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: A Definition of Done gives everyone a shared understanding of what Done means.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Having a common language.
choices.explanation: A common language avoids misunderstandings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Having a comprehensive documentation.
choices.explanation: Comprehensive documentation is not what creates transparency.

questions.question:
What is ATDD?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Using Acceptance Tests to define requirements specified by the customer and market.
choices.explanation: ATDD expresses requirements as acceptance tests that reflect customer and market expectations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Using advanced Integration Test to develop quality Product.
choices.explanation: ATDD is about acceptance tests, not integration tests.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Using approved tests by Product Owner in TDD.
choices.explanation: ATDD does not mean tests approved by the Product Owner.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Using Unit Tests to define requirements specified by the customer and market.
choices.explanation: Unit tests express technical requirements, not customer requirements.

questions.question:
In Software Development, which acronym is NOT true?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: LOC: Lines of Code.
choices.explanation: LOC does mean Lines of Code.

choices.label: B
choices.text: CBO: Coupling Between Objects.
choices.explanation: CBO does mean Coupling Between Objects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: DIT: Depth of Inheritance Tree.
choices.explanation: DIT does mean Depth of Inheritance Tree.

choices.label: D
choices.text: SLOC: Sample Lines of Code.
choices.explanation: SLOC means Source Lines of Code, not Sample Lines of Code.

questions.question:
Where does Smoke testing originate from?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Comes from a comprehensive type of hardware testing in which a device passes the test if it does not catch fire during a sample long time run.
choices.explanation: Smoke tests are basic, not comprehensive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Comes from a basic type of hardware testing in which a device passes the test if it does not catch fire during a sample long time run.
choices.explanation: Smoke tests check the first switch-on, not a long run.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Comes from a basic type of hardware testing in which a device passes the test if it does not catch fire the first time it turns on.
choices.explanation: Smoke testing comes from checking that a device does not catch fire when first powered on.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Comes from a comprehensive type of hardware testing in which a device passes the test if it does not catch fire the first time it turns on.
choices.explanation: Smoke tests are basic, not comprehensive.

questions.question:
What is the goal of the Continuous Integration?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: To publish the Product Increment on Production.
choices.explanation: Publishing to production is deployment, not the goal of CI.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To penalize the Developer who breaks the build.
choices.explanation: CI is not about blaming people.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To provide rapid feedback of build and test result.
choices.explanation: CI gives rapid feedback on build and test results after every change.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To find who has made the change on source control.
choices.explanation: Version control already shows who made a change.

questions.question:
What kind of activity can be done in the Product Backlog Refinement?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adding detail to the items.
choices.explanation: Refinement adds details such as description, order and size.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ordering.
choices.explanation: Ordering is part of refinement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Design.
choices.explanation: Design is done when implementing the work, even if some design thinking happens during refinement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Develop.
choices.explanation: Development happens during the Sprint, not during refinement.

questions.question:
Which one is true about the scaled Scrum?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The scaled Scrum does not add or change anything in Scrum framework.
choices.explanation: Scaling frameworks add practices on top of Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is based on the Scrum framework.
choices.explanation: Scaled Scrum is based on the Scrum framework.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It uses Scrum parts as its building blocks.
choices.explanation: Scaled Scrum uses Scrum Teams and Scrum elements as building blocks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Through scaled Scrum Teams work on multiple Products.
choices.explanation: Scaling is about multiple teams on one product, not teams on multiple products.

questions.question:
Which factors should be considered to determine the Sprint length?
(choose the best four answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Market change speed.
choices.explanation: Fast-changing markets call for shorter Sprints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Raising complexity speed.
choices.explanation: Growing complexity calls for more frequent inspection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Amount of the risk.
choices.explanation: Higher risk calls for shorter Sprints.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cost of risk.
choices.explanation: The cost of risk influences how often to inspect.

questions.question: True or False: One of the outcomes of using TDD is creating an automated Regression Test suite.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: TDD produces an automated suite that can be used as regression tests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The tests written in TDD become an automated regression test suite.

questions.question:
Which work can be done between two Sprints?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nothing. There is no special time between two Sprints.
choices.explanation: There is no time between Sprints; the next one starts immediately.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Resolving some important bugs.
choices.explanation: Bugs are handled within Sprints.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Preparing Product Backlog Items for the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Refinement happens within the Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thinking about architectural concerns of the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Architecture is addressed within Sprints.

questions.question:
How often should Sprint Planning be conducted?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Once a Release.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning happens every Sprint, not every release.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each time that the Product Owner decides.
choices.explanation: It is not decided by the Product Owner; it starts every Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the middle of each Sprint.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning starts the Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Once a Sprint.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning happens once per Sprint, at its start.

questions.question:
Which is NOT true about the Lines of Code metric?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A high count might indicate that a type or method is doing too much work.
choices.explanation: A high count may indicate too much responsibility; this is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A high count might be a warning that code will be hard to maintain.
choices.explanation: A high count may indicate maintainability problems; this is true.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It isn't a Code Quality metric.
choices.explanation: Lines of code is a size metric rather than a quality metric; this is true.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is explained via percentage.
choices.explanation: Lines of code is an absolute count, not a percentage.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for monitoring progress toward the Product Goal and within the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Product progress: the Product Owner, Sprint progress: the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner monitors progress toward the Product Goal; the Developers monitor progress within the Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Product progress: the Scrum Master, Sprint progress: the Developers.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not monitor overall progress.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Product progress: the Developers, Sprint progress: the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The roles are reversed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Product progress: the Product Owner, Sprint progress: the Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not monitor Sprint progress; the Developers do.

questions.question:
Which is true about Strategic Debt in Technical Debt context?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Debt caused to gain strategic benefits (such as time to market).
choices.explanation: Strategic debt is taken deliberately to gain benefits such as time to market.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This is typically caused by lack of awareness or knowledge.
choices.explanation: Debt caused by lack of knowledge is unintentional debt.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Short-time gains, for instance cutting some corners to make an extra release for increased customer satisfaction.
choices.explanation: Cutting corners for short-term gains is tactical debt.

questions.question:
Which one is a code metric?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Code Coverage.
choices.explanation: Code coverage is a test metric, not a code metric.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lines of Code.
choices.explanation: Lines of code is a code metric.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Automated Build.
choices.explanation: Automated build is a practice, not a metric.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Test Doubles.
choices.explanation: Test doubles are a testing technique, not a metric.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Class Coupling.
choices.explanation: Class coupling is a code metric.

questions.question:
What are the outputs of the Sprint Planning?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Increment.
choices.explanation: The Increment is created during the Sprint, not at Sprint Planning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Release Plan.
choices.explanation: There is no release plan in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning produces the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Sprint Goal.
choices.explanation: Sprint Planning produces the Sprint Goal, part of the Sprint Backlog.

questions.question: True or False: Dependency Inversion principle implies that entities must depend on abstractions not on concretions.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: This statement of the Dependency Inversion Principle is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: High-level and low-level modules both depend on abstractions, not on concrete implementations.

questions.question:
What will happen for the undone Sprint Backlog Items at the end of the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Extend the Sprint to finish them.
choices.explanation: Sprints are never extended.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move back to the bottom of the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Items return to the Product Backlog to be ordered by the Product Owner, not necessarily at the bottom.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Re-estimate and move back to the Product Backlog.
choices.explanation: Undone items go back to the Product Backlog with an updated estimate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Directly move to the next Sprint.
choices.explanation: Undone items do not automatically go to the next Sprint.

questions.question:
What should the Developers do when the CEO assigns them unplanned work in the middle of the Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inform the Scrum Master so he/she can work with the CEO.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner, not the Scrum Master, decides about the scope.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reject it because they are independent.
choices.explanation: Developers should not just reject; the request goes to the Product Owner.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accept it because the CEO is the highest rank in the organization.
choices.explanation: Hierarchy does not override the Product Owner's decisions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inform the Product Owner so he/she can work with the CEO.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner decides how to handle new requests.

questions.question:
When can the Developers change their practices, tools or techniques?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever needed.
choices.explanation: Developers can adapt their practices whenever they need to.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the end of each release.
choices.explanation: Improvement is not limited to the end of a release.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the beginning of the project.
choices.explanation: Improvement is continuous, not only at the beginning.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At the end of each Sprint.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is a formal opportunity, but improvements can happen any time.

questions.question:
Which two of the following are synonyms of TDD?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Domain Driven Design.
choices.explanation: Domain Driven Design is a design approach, not TDD.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Red-Green-Refactor.
choices.explanation: Red-Green-Refactor describes the TDD cycle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Test First Development (TFD).
choices.explanation: Test First Development is a synonym of TDD.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continuous Deployment.
choices.explanation: Continuous Deployment is a delivery practice.

questions.question:
When should tests be added in the development process?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the end of each release.
choices.explanation: Testing at the end delays feedback.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From the beginning of the project.
choices.explanation: Tests should be written from the beginning, continuously.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the end each Sprint.
choices.explanation: Testing at the end of each Sprint delays feedback within the Sprint.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In special Sprints called “Test Sprint”.
choices.explanation: There are no Test Sprints in Scrum.

questions.question:
Which language is usually used in BDD?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ubiquitous language.
choices.explanation: BDD uses a ubiquitous language shared by business and technical people.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tongue language.
choices.explanation: This is not a term used in BDD.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Technical language.
choices.explanation: BDD avoids purely technical language.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Native language.
choices.explanation: Native language is not the point; the shared domain language is.

questions.question:
Why are mock objects used in Unit Tests?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: To simulate the behavior of a given object.
choices.explanation: Mocks simulate the behavior of real objects.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To isolate system under test for controlled testing.
choices.explanation: Mocks isolate the system under test.

choices.label: C
choices.text: To cope with dependencies.
choices.explanation: Mocks replace dependencies that are hard to use in tests.

choices.label: D
choices.text: TDD can be done just by having mock objects.
choices.explanation: Mocks are a tool; TDD is not done just by having them.

questions.question:
Which is NOT true about Efferent Coupling?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Classes with high efferent will affect other classes when changes are made.
choices.explanation: This is not true: a class with high efferent coupling is affected by changes in others; affecting others is afferent coupling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A large Efferent Coupling can indicate that a class is unfocused and may also indicate that it is unstable since it depends on the stability of all the types to which it is coupled.
choices.explanation: This statement about efferent coupling is true.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Classes with high Efferent Coupling will receive the effects of changes or defects in other classes.
choices.explanation: This statement about efferent coupling is true.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a Code Quality metric.
choices.explanation: Efferent coupling is indeed a code quality metric.

questions.question:
What is the instability index metric calculation formula? (Ca: Afferent Coupling, Ce: Efferent Coupling)
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ca / (Ca+Ce).
choices.explanation: This is the inverse of the instability formula.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ce / (Ca+Ce).
choices.explanation: Instability is Ce / (Ca + Ce): the share of outgoing dependencies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: (Ca+Ce) / Ce.
choices.explanation: This formula is not used.

choices.label: D
choices.text: (Ca+Ce) / Ca.
choices.explanation: This formula is not used.

questions.question:
Which principle is included in SOLID?
(choose the best four answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Liskov Substitution Principle.
choices.explanation: Liskov Substitution is the L in SOLID.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dual Interface Principle.
choices.explanation: There is no Dual Interface Principle in SOLID.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Single Responsibility Principle.
choices.explanation: Single Responsibility is the S in SOLID.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Open-Closed Principle.
choices.explanation: Open-Closed is the O in SOLID.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Interface Segregation Principle.
choices.explanation: Interface Segregation is the I in SOLID.

questions.question: True or False: In an impediment case, the Scrum Master can intervene to help the Developers to remove a member from the Developers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master can help resolve such impediments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master can help the Developers address an issue with a member, as an impediment.

questions.question:
Which one is true about the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is a feedback loop.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is an inspection and adaptation feedback loop.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All Scrum Team members should participate in it.
choices.explanation: Only the Developers are required.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers monitor Sprint progress toward the Sprint Goal.
choices.explanation: The Developers inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is a 15 minutes time-box event.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is timeboxed to 15 minutes.

questions.question:
What are traits of a high performance Scrum Team?
(choose the best four answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: They live the Scrum Values deeply.
choices.explanation: High-performing teams live the Scrum values.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They help their customers become more successful.
choices.explanation: They focus on making their customers successful.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They evolve the Definition of Done over time and add more stringent criteria to it continuously.
choices.explanation: They continuously strengthen their Definition of Done.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There is a high level of creativity, productivity and accountability in the Team dynamics.
choices.explanation: They show creativity, productivity and accountability.

choices.label: E
choices.text: They respect top managers through accepting their work every time.
choices.explanation: Accepting all work from managers is not a trait of high performance.

questions.question:
Who knows best about how to create usable and releasable Increments?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: Developers know best how to turn Product Backlog items into usable Increments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master does not decide how the work is done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Technical Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Technical Manager.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner knows what is valuable, but not how to build it.

questions.question: True or False: Interface Segregation principle implies that a client should never be forced to implement an interface that it doesn't use.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: This statement of the Interface Segregation Principle is true.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Clients should not depend on methods they do not use.

questions.question:
Who is responsible for the Product Backlog Items and tasks estimation in Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing product value, not tracking remaining Sprint work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Scrum Master.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master facilitates Scrum but is not accountable for tracking remaining Sprint work.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: The Project Manager role is not defined in Scrum and does not track Sprint work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers are accountable for managing and tracking progress toward the Sprint Goal.

questions.question: True or False: Through the Sprint Review, the Scrum Team tries to hand-off the Increment to the Customer formally.

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is a working session, not a formal hand-off.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review is not a formal acceptance or hand-off.

questions.question:
Which Scrum Values are adhered by not building Product Backlog Items that have low business value?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Courage.
choices.explanation: Courage is needed to say no to low-value work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Respect.
choices.explanation: Respecting stakeholders means not wasting their money.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Focus.
choices.explanation: Focus means working on the most valuable things.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transparency.
choices.explanation: Transparency is a pillar, not a value.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adaptation.
choices.explanation: Adaptation is a pillar, not a value.

questions.question:
Which one is true about Design Patterns?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Is a general, reusable solution to a commonly occurring problem within a given context in Software Design.
choices.explanation: A design pattern is a general reusable solution to a common problem in a context.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Is a low-fidelity UI pattern that can be called sketch.
choices.explanation: Sketches are UI artifacts, not design patterns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Is a list of guidelines to design better UX for customers.
choices.explanation: UX guidelines are not design patterns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Is a high-fidelity UI pattern that can be called prototype.
choices.explanation: Prototypes are UI artifacts, not design patterns.

questions.question:
Which Scrum events can use more time rather than their time-box if there are 9 Developers in the Team?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum timebox applies whatever the team size.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sprint Retrospective.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Retrospective timebox applies whatever the team size.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No one.
choices.explanation: Timeboxes are maximums that apply whatever the team size.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: The Sprint Review timebox applies whatever the team size.

questions.question:
Select the desirable characteristics of a Unit Test.
(choose the best four answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Code in each test is as small as possible while maintaining readability of the code.
choices.explanation: Small test code stays readable and focused.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each test is independent of other Unit Tests.
choices.explanation: Independent tests can run in any order.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each test makes assertions about only one logical concept.
choices.explanation: One logical concept per test makes failures clear.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The test executes fast.
choices.explanation: Fast tests can be run often.

choices.label: E
choices.text: They exercise the persistence layer of a solution.
choices.explanation: Unit tests should not depend on the persistence layer.

questions.question:
Should User Stories be part of the documentation generated by a Scrum project?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Always.
choices.explanation: Documentation is not always needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the Architect requires it.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no architect deciding documentation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If they are part of the Definition of Done.
choices.explanation: If the Definition of Done requires them, they are part of the documentation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Never.
choices.explanation: They may be useful; it depends on the Definition of Done.

choices.label: E
choices.text: They must be provided to the Developers as part of the user specifications documents.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require upfront specification documents.

questions.question:
The Definition of Done describes the work that must be completed for every Product Backlog Item before it can be deemed releasable. What should the Developers do when, during the Sprint, they find out that a problem outside of their control blocks them from doing all this work?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cancel the Sprint.
choices.explanation: Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Complete the work that can be done on as much scope as possible and complete the rest during the "hardening" Sprints at the end of the release.
choices.explanation: There are no hardening Sprints.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Complete the work that can be done on as much scope as possible and use the Sprint Review to plan the rest with the Stakeholders.
choices.explanation: Undone work cannot be planned for later with stakeholders.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Immediately raise the issue to the Scrum Master as an impediment.
choices.explanation: The issue should be raised immediately to the Scrum Master as an impediment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Stop using Scrum.
choices.explanation: Stopping Scrum is not a solution.

questions.question:
To refine Product Backlog Items, the following activities will occur implicitly or explicitly:
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Analysis.
choices.explanation: Refinement includes analysis of the items.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decomposition.
choices.explanation: Refinement includes decomposing items into smaller ones.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Design.
choices.explanation: Refinement includes some design thinking to understand the work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Programming.
choices.explanation: Programming is done during the Sprint, not during refinement.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testing.
choices.explanation: Testing is done during the Sprint, not during refinement.

questions.question: True or False: Only technical writers can create documentation during a Sprint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Anyone in the Developers can create documentation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Technical Writer role; the Developers create documentation.

questions.question: True or False: The Scrum Team should choose at least one high priority process improvement, identified during the Sprint Retrospective, and place it in the Product Backlog.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: There is no such obligation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team may add improvements to the Sprint Backlog, but there is no obligation.

questions.question:
What are some shortcomings of Code Coverage as a measurement for how well a system or Product is tested?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Code Coverage does not ensure that the most important or highest risk areas of the code are being exercised by tests.
choices.explanation: Coverage does not show whether the most important or risky code is tested.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Code Coverage does not necessarily provide functional coverage.
choices.explanation: Coverage does not show functional coverage.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Code Coverage metrics vary by development platform (e.g., .NET, Java).
choices.explanation: Platform differences are not a fundamental shortcoming.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Could create incentives to write tests that simply increase Code Coverage, rather than tests that find bugs without increasing coverage.
choices.explanation: Targets can encourage tests that increase coverage rather than find bugs.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is too complicated to explain to Management.
choices.explanation: Complexity is not the issue.

questions.question:
What are three advantages of Continuous Integration?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Broken builds are detected quickly.
choices.explanation: CI detects broken builds quickly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Know immediately how a check-in affected the build.
choices.explanation: CI shows immediately how a change affects the build.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Readability of code is improved.
choices.explanation: CI does not directly improve readability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Software is generally kept in a buildable state.
choices.explanation: CI keeps the software in a buildable state.

questions.question:
What are ways the Developers can ensure a good Application Architecture?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers don't need an architecture model in Scrum and should focus on adding functionality. The architecture will come into place without fail as the Developers add functionality.
choices.explanation: Architecture does not appear by itself; it requires deliberate attention.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Developers plan a Sprint 0 at the beginning of a project with the objective of developing an architecture model used during the following Sprints.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0 in Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Developers plan some time each Sprint to discuss the architecture needed for the features planned in that Sprint.
choices.explanation: Discussing architecture each Sprint keeps it adapted to the work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers should assign someone to the role of Software Architect whose job it is to make sure a consistent architecture is developed.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Software Architect role.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Developers should have a set of guiding architecture principles that every Developer understands and follows when writing code.
choices.explanation: Shared architecture principles keep design consistent.

questions.question:
What does a test written with Test Driven Development represent?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A bug that will be uncovered.
choices.explanation: A TDD test describes behavior, not a bug.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A technical requirement that must be satisfied.
choices.explanation: A TDD test expresses a technical requirement the code must satisfy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An assignment from the lead quality engineer.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no lead quality engineer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Something that completes the test coverage of a system.
choices.explanation: Coverage is a side effect, not what the test represents.

questions.question:
What does Code Coverage show?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Code being exercised by tests.
choices.explanation: Coverage shows which code is exercised by tests.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The absence of defects in code.
choices.explanation: Coverage does not prove the absence of defects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The quality of Unit Tests being written.
choices.explanation: Coverage does not measure test quality.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ratio of number of tests to lines of code in the system being tested.
choices.explanation: Coverage is not a ratio of tests to lines of code.

choices.label: E
choices.text: When a feature is done.
choices.explanation: Coverage does not say when a feature is done.

questions.question:
What is a Unit Test?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A technique for ensuring that units of co-dependent or clustered computers perform correctly.
choices.explanation: This is not what a unit test is.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A test that isolates and verifies individual units of source code.
choices.explanation: A unit test isolates and verifies an individual unit of source code.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A way for the team to ensure that the system satisfies the user requirements.
choices.explanation: Checking user requirements is acceptance testing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A way in which units of programmers ensure their code works.
choices.explanation: Unit tests test units of code, not of programmers.

questions.question:
What is Code Coverage?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: An insurance policy that covers the code for defects.
choices.explanation: Coverage is not an insurance policy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The degree to which the system under test has been exercised by tests.
choices.explanation: Code coverage measures how much of the system is exercised by tests.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The number of Developers that understand how the code works.
choices.explanation: Coverage is not about people's understanding.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The percent of code in version control included in a build.
choices.explanation: Coverage is not about builds.

questions.question:
What is Technical Debt?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A term representing the eventual consequences of poor technical choices.
choices.explanation: Technical debt is the eventual consequence of poor or expedient technical choices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Code that has not been commented or documented.
choices.explanation: Missing comments are only one possible form.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average time or money a Scrum Team spends per Sprint on bug fixes.
choices.explanation: It is not a measure of time spent on bug fixes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The money an organization owes to tool and hardware vendors.
choices.explanation: It is not about financial debt.

questions.question:
What relationship does Scrum have to technical practices?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: All technical practices must be used to support Scrum.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require all technical practices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Developers with excellent technical practices will likely be more successful.
choices.explanation: Excellent technical practices help teams succeed with Scrum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scrum requires specific technical practices or it isn't Scrum.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not require specific technical practices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: None.
choices.explanation: Technical practices strongly support Scrum.

questions.question:
When are Testers and quality experts ideally included in a project?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: After Developer handoff.
choices.explanation: Testing after hand-off delays feedback.

choices.label: B
choices.text: After Sprint Review.
choices.explanation: Testing after the Sprint Review means the work was not Done.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From the beginning and throughout all Sprints.
choices.explanation: Quality skills are needed from the beginning and throughout all Sprints.

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the Product is feature complete.
choices.explanation: Waiting for feature completeness delays feedback.

questions.question:
When is a System's Architecture decided?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the beginning of the project, during Sprint 0.
choices.explanation: There is no Sprint 0.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is designed along with the vision, before the first Sprint.
choices.explanation: Architecture is not fully designed before the first Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Throughout the project, as understanding emerges and the Developers learn more about the project.
choices.explanation: Architecture is decided throughout the project as understanding emerges.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whenever the assigned Architect can join the Developers.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Architect role.

questions.question:
Which of the following are benefits of Continuous Integration?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Causes team members to consider each other's work and context.
choices.explanation: Integrating frequently makes team members aware of each other's work.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It eliminates bugs completely.
choices.explanation: CI does not eliminate bugs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It leads to higher transparency and rapid feedback to the team.
choices.explanation: CI brings transparency and rapid feedback.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The build is executed once every night and at least once each weekend.
choices.explanation: Nightly builds are not continuous integration.

questions.question:
Which of the following are NOT metrics of Code Quality?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Class Coupling.
choices.explanation: Class coupling is a code quality metric.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Code Coverage.
choices.explanation: Code coverage is a test metric, not a code quality metric.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cycle Time per Feature.
choices.explanation: Cycle time is a flow metric, not a code quality metric.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cyclomatic Complexity.
choices.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity is a code quality metric.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Depth of Inheritance.
