choices.explanation: Depth of inheritance is a code quality metric.

questions.question:
Which of the following best describes Continuous Integration?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A Software Development practice that continuously integrates feedback from users into Software Design.
choices.explanation: This describes user feedback, not CI.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A Software Development practice used by Integration Teams to create Best Practice branching and merging strategies.
choices.explanation: CI is not about integration teams.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A Software Development practice where members of the Developers all work on the same computer to ensure a common code base.
choices.explanation: CI does not mean sharing a computer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A Software Development practice where members of the Developers integrate and verify their work frequently, often multiple times each day, to detect integration errors as quickly as possible.
choices.explanation: CI means integrating and verifying work frequently to detect errors quickly.

questions.question:
Which of the following describe an Architecture Spike?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A decision made by a Systems Architect to settle disagreement within the Developers.
choices.explanation: A spike is not a decision by an architect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A fundamental architectural problem found in an existing application.
choices.explanation: A spike is not a problem; it is an activity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A small development activity to learn about technical elements of a proposed solution.
choices.explanation: A spike is a small development activity to learn about technical elements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The result of an exhaustive architectural planning effort.
choices.explanation: A spike is small, not exhaustive.

questions.question:
Which statements describe why automated builds are important?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: They allow frequent validation of the unit of Software being worked on, ensuring it remains in a potentially shippable state.
choices.explanation: Automated builds validate the software often, keeping it potentially releasable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The build process is clearly defined and scripted, making it easy consistent and repeatable.
choices.explanation: A scripted build is consistent and repeatable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They eliminate the need for Build Engineers.
choices.explanation: They do not necessarily eliminate roles.

choices.label: D
choices.text: They ensure your Product remains bug free.
choices.explanation: Builds do not ensure bug-free products.

choices.label: E
choices.text: They support continuous integration.
choices.explanation: Automated builds are the foundation of continuous integration.

questions.question:
You are on a Scrum Team that is enhancing an existing Product. Which is the LEAST useful piece of documentation you want to have at your disposal?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acceptance Tests.
choices.explanation: Acceptance tests document expected behavior.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Detailed designs.
choices.explanation: Detailed designs can be useful when enhancing a product.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The full history of retrospective plans and lessons learned.
choices.explanation: The history of retrospectives is the least useful to enhance a product.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Well-structured and named code.
choices.explanation: Well-structured code is the most reliable documentation.

questions.question: True or False: Test Driven Development is a predictable way to develop working, well-organized code?

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: TDD does not make development predictable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: TDD improves design and feedback, but does not make development predictable.

questions.question:
Who determines when it is appropriate to update the Sprint Backlog during a Sprint?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: The Developers own the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Project Manager.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Project Manager.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Product Owner.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner does not update the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Developers.
choices.explanation: The Developers update their Sprint Backlog whenever needed.

questions.question:
What is the Scrum Master responsible for during the Sprint Retrospective?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Summarizing and reporting the discussions to management.
choices.explanation: The Retrospective is not a reporting meeting for management.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Acting as a scribe to capture the Scrum Team's answers.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master is not a scribe.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Participating as a Scrum Team member and facilitating as requested or needed.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master participates as a team member and facilitates when needed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prioritizing the resulting action items.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Team prioritizes its own improvements.

questions.question:
The right time to refactor code using Test Driven Development is:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: When I can see the "debt" building in the code.
choices.explanation: Refactoring is part of each TDD cycle, not only when debt is visible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When preparing legacy code for unit tests.
choices.explanation: Legacy code is another context.

choices.label: C
choices.text: After the test passes.
choices.explanation: In TDD you refactor after the test passes (red, green, refactor).

choices.label: D
choices.text: After the test fails.
choices.explanation: After the test fails, you write code to make it pass.

questions.question:
Why is architectural layering important for emergent systems?
(choose the best three answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Layering makes it easier to reuse functionality.
choices.explanation: Layering eases reuse of functionality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Layering assigns clear responsibilities to individual Developers.
choices.explanation: Layering does not assign responsibilities to people.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Layering separates different logical concerns within the system.
choices.explanation: Layering separates logical concerns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Layering increases maintainability of a system by isolating functional responsibilities.
choices.explanation: Layering improves maintainability by isolating responsibilities.

questions.question:
Is it a good idea to follow each automated build with the execution of automated tests?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. Code Coverage can be used to assess progress.
choices.explanation: Coverage is not a measure of progress.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No. Automated tests should be executed when the implementation of a Product Backlog item is complete.
choices.explanation: Tests should run after each build, not only when items are complete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes. The tests may identify whether there are problems that the Developers should fix before proceeding.
choices.explanation: Running tests after each build reveals problems immediately.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No. It would take too much time.
choices.explanation: Automated tests are designed to run fast and often.

questions.question:
What is Pair Programming?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Developers that are able to write code both in the back-end and the front-end.
choices.explanation: This is about skills, not pairing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two Developers working on the same problem, at the same computer (physically or virtually), at the same time.
choices.explanation: Pair programming is two Developers working on the same problem at the same time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two persons working on the same Product Backlog item trying to get it one as soon as possible.
choices.explanation: Working on the same item is not pairing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A Tester and a Developer working together to ensure high quality.
choices.explanation: Pairing is between Developers, not a Tester and a Developer.

questions.question:
Which best describes the practice of branching code in a version control system?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tagging or labelling a particular codebase as ready for distribution.
choices.explanation: Tagging marks a version.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Creating a duplicate of existing code, isolated from the original code.
choices.explanation: Branching duplicates code into an isolated line of development.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Releasing a specific codebase into a production environment.
choices.explanation: Releasing is deployment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Combining two or more branches of code into a single codebase.
choices.explanation: Combining branches is merging.

questions.question:
Cyclomatic Complexity is a metric for:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assessing if code is written in as few lines as possible.
choices.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity is not about the number of lines.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A measurement for complexity based on the number of people involved.
choices.explanation: It is not about people.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Determining the number of unit tests required to ensure correctness.
choices.explanation: It indicates a minimum number of test paths, but does not ensure correctness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Demonstrating code is well-structured and cleanly implemented.
choices.explanation: It does not demonstrate clean code.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Measuring branching structures and nesting levels in code.
choices.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity measures branching and nesting in code.

questions.question:
The Developers should have all the skills needed to:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Complete the project as estimated when the date and cost are committed to the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not about committing dates and costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn the Product Backlog items they select into an Increment of useful and valuable product functionality.
choices.explanation: The Developers have all the skills to turn selected items into a useful Increment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Do all of the development work, except for specialized testing that requires additional tools and environments.
choices.explanation: There is no exception for specialized testing; testing is part of Done.

questions.question:
Which statement best describes Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: A framework for creating complex products in complex environments.
choices.explanation: Scrum is a framework for creating complex products in complex environments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A defined and predictive process that conforms to the principles of Scientific Management.
choices.explanation: Scrum is empirical, not defined or predictive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A complete methodology that defines how to develop software.
choices.explanation: Scrum is a framework, not a complete methodology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A cookbook that defines best practices for software development.
choices.explanation: Scrum is not a cookbook.

questions.question:
The timebox for a Daily Scrum is?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: The Daily Scrum is timeboxed to 15 minutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: 15 minutes for a 4-week sprint. For shorter Sprints it is usually shorter.
choices.explanation: It is 15 minutes regardless of Sprint length.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two minutes per person.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not define two minutes per person.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 4 hours.
choices.explanation: Four hours is the Sprint Review timebox.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The same time of day every day.
choices.explanation: This describes consistency, not a timebox.

questions.question:
The Developers should not be interrupted during the Sprint and the Sprint Goal should remain intact. These are conditions that foster creativity, quality and productivity. Which one of the following answers is FALSE?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Developers may work with the Product Owner to add or remove work if they find themselves with more or less capacity than expected.
choices.explanation: This statement is true; scope can be adjusted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Sprint Backlog is fully formulated in the Sprint Planning event and does not change during the Sprint.
choices.explanation: This statement is false: the Sprint Backlog emerges during the Sprint.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As a decomposition of the selected Product Backlog items, the Sprint Backlog changes and may grow as the work emerges.
choices.explanation: This statement is true; the Sprint Backlog changes as work emerges.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Product Owner can help clarify or optimize the Sprint when asked by the Developers.
choices.explanation: This statement is true; the Product Owner can help clarify.

questions.question:
The three pillars of empiricism are:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Respect For People, Kaizen, Eliminating Waste.
choices.explanation: These are Lean principles, not Scrum pillars.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Planning, Inspection, Adaptation.
choices.explanation: Planning is not a pillar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Planning, Demonstration, Retrospective.
choices.explanation: These are not pillars.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inspection, Transparency, Adaptation.
choices.explanation: Transparency, inspection and adaptation are the three pillars of empiricism.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transparency, Eliminating Waste, Kaizen.
choices.explanation: Eliminating waste and Kaizen are Lean concepts.

questions.question:
What is the function or purpose of Management in Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Identify and remove people that are not working hard enough.
choices.explanation: Management does not monitor individuals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monitor the progress of the Developers on the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Management does not monitor the Developers' progress.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Support the Product Owner with insights and information into high value product and system capabilities. Support the Scrum Master to encourage organizational change that fosters empiricism, self-management, bottom-up intelligence, and intelligent product delivery.
choices.explanation: Management supports the Product Owner and the Scrum Master in enabling empiricism and self-management.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continually monitor staffing levels of the Scrum Team.
choices.explanation: Monitoring staffing is not management's purpose in Scrum.

questions.question:
What is the main reason for the Scrum Master to be at the Daily Scrum?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: To gather status and progress information to report to management.
choices.explanation: Status reporting to management is not the purpose of the Daily Scrum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: To write down any changes to the Sprint Backlog, including adding new items, and tracking progress on the burn-down.
choices.explanation: The Developers maintain the Sprint Backlog.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They do not have to be there; they only need to ensure the Developers have a Daily Scrum.
choices.explanation: The Scrum Master only ensures the Daily Scrum takes place; attendance is not required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: To make sure every team member answers the three questions.
choices.explanation: The three questions are not mandatory.

questions.question:
Which two things should the Scrum Team do during the first Sprint?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Develop and deliver at least one piece of functionality.
choices.explanation: Every Sprint, including the first, delivers at least one piece of functionality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Develop a plan for the rest of the release.
choices.explanation: Planning the rest of the release upfront is not empirical.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deliver an Increment of useful and valuable product.
choices.explanation: Every Sprint delivers a valuable, useful Increment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Determine the complete architecture and infrastructure for the product.
choices.explanation: Architecture emerges; it is not determined upfront.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create the complete Product Backlog to be developed in subsequent Sprints.
choices.explanation: The Product Backlog is never complete.

questions.question: True or False: It is mandatory that the product Increment be released to production at the end of each Sprint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Releasing is a Product Owner decision; it is not mandatory every Sprint.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: An Increment must be usable, but whether to release it is a business decision.

questions.question:
When should a Developer on a Scrum Team be replaced?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: As needed, with no special allowance for changes in productivity.
choices.explanation: Changes have a cost; ignoring the short-term productivity drop is unrealistic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every Sprint to promote shared learning.
choices.explanation: Changing members every Sprint disrupts the team and lowers productivity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As needed, while taking into account a short-term reduction in productivity.
choices.explanation: Membership can change when needed, while accepting the short-term reduction in productivity it causes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Never, it reduces productivity.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not forbid changes; sometimes they are needed.

questions.question:
Refactoring is:
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Improving your code without breaking your unit tests.
choices.explanation: Refactoring improves code while keeping its behavior, so the unit tests keep passing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing the amount of code.
choices.explanation: Refactoring is not about increasing code.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multiplying the amount of code.
choices.explanation: Refactoring is not about multiplying code.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reducing the amount of code.
choices.explanation: Reducing code can be a result, but it is not the definition.

questions.question:
Developers include which role(s)?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Software Architects.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no architect role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Business Analysts.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no business analyst role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Testers.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no tester role.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No other roles. Developer is one of the 3 accountabilities in Scrum.
choices.explanation: Developers is one of the three accountabilities; Scrum recognizes no sub-roles.

questions.question: True or False: The more code a Developer writes the better.

choices.label: A
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: More code means more to maintain; value matters, not quantity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: The amount of code is not a measure of value or quality.

questions.question:
How much time must a Product Owner spend with the Developers?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Scrum does not prescribe a fixed percentage of time for the Product Owner.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enough so that the Product Owner is not surprised by the value delivered by the Increment.
choices.explanation: The Product Owner collaborates as much as needed so that the Increment delivers the expected value; Scrum defines accountability, not a fixed time allocation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 40%, or more if the Stakeholders agree.
choices.explanation: Scrum does not define any percentage, and stakeholders do not decide the Product Owner's availability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any amount of time the Developers ask the Product Owner to be present.
choices.explanation: The Developers do not set the Product Owner's presence; the Product Owner engages as needed to maximize value.

questions.question:
When a Continuous Integration build fails, who ideally ensures the build is repaired?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The person who broke the build.
choices.explanation: Usually the person who broke the build repairs it, but the self-managing Developers can organize differently.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The next person who needs the build to complete successfully.
choices.explanation: Leaving the fix to whoever needs it next delays the repair; fixing a broken build is a priority for the team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The person assigned to the configuration management role within the team.
choices.explanation: Scrum recognizes no sub-roles among Developers; the build is a shared responsibility.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Tester responsible for validating builds.
choices.explanation: Scrum has no Tester role; quality is the Developers' responsibility.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whoever the Developers agree should fix it.
choices.explanation: The self-managing Developers decide who repairs the build; often the person who broke it, but they are free to organize otherwise.

questions.question:
What are the duties of the Developers in a Scrum Team?
(choose the best two answers)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Removing impediments.
choices.explanation: Causing the removal of impediments is a service of the Scrum Master, even if Developers can solve many problems themselves.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Making technical decisions.
choices.explanation: The Developers decide how to turn Product Backlog items into a usable Increment, including technical decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resolving team internal conflicts.
choices.explanation: Conflicts are handled by the self-managing Scrum Team as a whole, with the Scrum Master's help if needed; it is not a specific duty of the Developers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sizing Product Backlog Items.
choices.explanation: The Developers who will do the work are responsible for sizing Product Backlog items.

questions.question:
While developing new functionality, you find a bug that has already been delivered to the customer. What do you do?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Revise the tests so that the bug no longer appears on the bug report.
choices.explanation: Hiding a bug by changing tests destroys transparency and quality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fix the bug.
choices.explanation: Delivered functionality is outside the current Sprint scope; the Product Owner decides how and when to address it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Talk to the Product Owner.
choices.explanation: A bug in already delivered work is new work: the Product Owner decides, with the Developers, how and when to handle it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stub out the code that caused the bug so it no longer occurs.
choices.explanation: Stubbing out code hides the problem and may break functionality.

questions.question: True or False: The Developers have immediately resolved a bug, which is found in the current Sprint and belongs to an Increment that has already been delivered to the market. Is it a proper behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: False.
choices.explanation: A bug in an already delivered Increment is new work; it should be discussed with the Product Owner, who decides how and when to address it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: True.
choices.explanation: Fixing it immediately bypasses the Product Owner, who orders the work, and can endanger the Sprint Goal.

questions.question:
What is the usual comparison of Product Backlog Items average size in the Product Backlog and Sprint Backlog?
(choose the best answer)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Product Backlog Items in the Product Backlog are usually smaller than the Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: Items are not systematically smaller in the Product Backlog.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Product Backlog Items in the Product Backlog are usually larger than the Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: Items in the Product Backlog are refined too, especially the higher-ordered ones; there is no systematic size difference.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Product Backlog Items usually have the same size in both the Product Backlog and the Sprint Backlog.
choices.explanation: Size varies with refinement and ordering; there is no rule that sizes are equal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Such a comparison does not make sense.
choices.explanation: Product Backlog items are refined continuously, whether they are in the Product Backlog or selected for the Sprint; comparing average sizes is not meaningful.
